column1: # IVE-X4R-DG1 — Edge Function deploy allowlist. Single source of truth,
# read by both .github/workflows/deploy-edge-functions.yml (the real
# deploy) and scripts/ci/resolve_deploy_selection.sh (the no-production
# dry-run test that proves the same logic without ever calling
# `supabase`). Do not duplicate this mapping anywhere else.
# Format: <function_name><TAB><jwt_flag>
#   jwt_flag empty  -> deploy WITHOUT --no-verify-jwt (JWT verification
#                      required; matches supabase/config.toml).
#   jwt_flag set    -> deploy WITH --no-verify-jwt (JWT verification
#                      disabled for this function; this workflow never
#                      turns JWT verification ON or OFF as a side effect
#                      of deploying -- it only ever preserves whatever
#                      policy is recorded here).
# IVE-COMMERCIAL-AUTH-01 (this change): every jwt_flag below was cleared.
# The 15 functions that previously carried --no-verify-jwt were found to
# have zero internal auth -- verify_jwt=false plus a shared, server-side
# GROQ_API_KEY meant any anonymous caller could consume paid AI capacity
# directly, bypassing the app. Codex's adversarial audit additionally
# found that verify_jwt=true alone is NOT sufficient proof of a real user
# (the public anon/publishable key is itself a validly-signed JWT and
# passes that platform gate) -- so the actual fail-closed boundary is
# supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts's resolveAuthenticatedUser(), which
# every one of these functions now calls before any Groq request. This
# file only controls the platform-level gate; do not treat an empty
# jwt_flag here as the whole story for any function without also
# checking that it imports and enforces the shared auth helper.
# Historical values (pre-AUTH-01, --no-verify-jwt) are preserved in git
# history -- see IVE-X4R-DG1 (docs/ive/X4R_DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.md) for why
# they were set that way originally, and the IVE-COMMERCIAL-AUTH-01
# Codex adversarial audit for the finding that closed them.
# Changing a function's JWT policy is a separate, explicit decision --
# edit this file deliberately and note why, never as a side effect of
# an unrelated deploy.
# Deliberately NOT listed (undeployable through this workflow):
#   ive-agent-runner  -- FROZEN. No source exists in this repository
#                        (confirmed absent from supabase/functions/ on
#                        both main and this branch); protected since
#                        X4A; the workflow also hard-blocks this name
#                        explicitly regardless of allowlist contents.
# process-file (IVE-PROCESS-FILE-CLOSURE): previously excluded here at
# ~91MB of bundled dependencies (confirmed via `deno info`, far worse
# than the ~33MB originally estimated) -- npm:pdf-parse transitively
# pulled in pdfjs-dist + a native @napi-rs/canvas renderer, purely to
# support PDF *rendering*, which this function's actual job (text
# extraction) never needed. Dropped pdf-parse entirely in favor of the
# regex-based extraction that was already the fallback path; bundle is
# now ~1.8MB, same order as every other function here. Also gained the
# same resolveAuthenticatedUser() gate as the rest of this list, plus an
# explicit pre-parse file-type and size ceiling it never had before.
